name: Go microservices with a gateway and a queue
summary: Small Go services, each owning its data, behind an API gateway; services talk synchronously over gRPC and asynchronously over NATS JetStream. Runs on Kubernetes with GitOps. For several teams that need to deploy independently.

fitsWhen.says: several teams need to deploy independently
Kubernetes or a big cloud is available
an API platform or a system of services

avoidWhen.says: one small team would run many services
the budget is tight (a cluster costs money every month)

backend.why: Small static binaries, fast start, low memory per service; concurrency in the standard library.

frontend.why: A separate web app talks only to the gateway.

database.why: One database (or schema) per service; no shared tables.

queue.why: JetStream gives durable subjects with far less to operate than Kafka.

auth.why: The gateway validates tokens so services receive a verified identity.

infra.why: Independent deploys, autoscaling and service discovery.

ci-cd.why: GitOps: a service's manifest change in git is the deployment.

observability.why: A trace must cross every service hop to debug anything.

testing.why: Contract and integration tests against real Postgres and NATS.

services.name: gateway
responsibilities: TLS, routing, token validation, rate limits

services.name: notifications
responsibilities: Consumes events and sends email and push

environments.name: dev
environments.purpose: A local cluster (kind or k3d) or docker compose with every service

environments.name: prod
environments.hosting: Managed Kubernetes, several nodes across zones

stages.name: image
stages.does: Build and push a signed image per changed service

stages.name: promote
stages.does: Update the image tag in the GitOps repository; Argo CD syncs

notes: Terraform for the cluster, databases and DNS
Trace context carried through NATS headers

security.auth: OIDC at the gateway; services trust only the gateway's verified headers, over mTLS inside the cluster
security.secrets: Kubernetes secrets from Vault or SOPS-encrypted files
notes: Each service has its own database credentials

conventions: A service owns its tables; nobody else reads them

adrs.title: Database per service
adrs.decision: Each service owns its schema and connection.
adrs.why: Independent deploys are impossible while services share tables.

adrs.title: NATS JetStream for events
adrs.why: Durable delivery and replay with one small binary to operate.
